title: Portal Wall
subtitle: MIT Media Lab · 1985 → 2026
_note: Placeholder entries sketched for the prototype. Verify every date/name and swap in real archive images (assets/img/<id>.jpg) and depth maps (assets/depth/<id>.png) before showing it. Optional per entry: 'video' (mp4), 'splat' (.ply/.splat/.ksplat for a Gaussian splat), 'depthScale' (0..1, default 0.35).

entries.title: The Media Lab opens
entries.blurb: Nicholas Negroponte and Jerome Wiesner open the Lab in I.M. Pei's E15, on the bet that computing, publishing and broadcast would converge.

entries.title: Put-That-There lineage
entries.blurb: Speech plus gesture, pointing at a wall-sized display. The direct ancestor of what your hands are doing right now.

entries.title: Things That Think
entries.blurb: Everyday objects get sensing and computation, years before anyone said 'Internet of Things'.

entries.title: Being Digital
entries.blurb: Bits, not atoms. The book that explained the Lab's worldview to everyone else.

entries.title: Tangible Bits
entries.blurb: Grasp and manipulate digital information through physical objects and surfaces.

entries.title: Affective Computing
entries.blurb: Machines that recognize, interpret and respond to human emotion. The field gets its name here.

entries.title: E Ink
entries.blurb: Electrophoretic paper leaves the Lab and ends up in every e-reader.

entries.title: LEGO Mindstorms
entries.blurb: The programmable brick: Papert's constructionism, boxed and sold.

entries.title: Minority Report
entries.blurb: The g-speak gestural interface seen in the film was designed by Media Lab alumni. This wall is a nod to it.

entries.title: One Laptop per Child
entries.blurb: The $100 laptop. Ambitious, contested, still shaping arguments about education technology.

entries.title: Scratch
entries.blurb: Block programming for kids, now one of the largest creative communities online.

entries.title: SixthSense
entries.blurb: A wearable projector and camera that turns any surface into an interface.

entries.title: Opera of the Future
entries.blurb: Hyperinstruments and city symphonies: music as an interface to collective memory.

entries.title: inFORM
entries.blurb: A shape display. Pins rise and fall so remote hands can push objects across a table.

entries.title: Open Agriculture
entries.blurb: Food computers and climate recipes: an experiment in open hardware for growing.

entries.title: Space Exploration Initiative
entries.blurb: Zero-g flights and payloads to the ISS. The Lab's research leaves the ground.

entries.title: Conformable Decoders
entries.blurb: Flexible electronics that read the body's mechanical signals.

entries.title: AI Companions
entries.blurb: Wearables and agents built to augment attention and memory instead of hijacking them.

entries.title: 40 Years
entries.blurb: Four decades of demos. This wall is one more.
